title: What is going on here, Microsoft?
body:
Am I the only one whose negative app review keeps getting removed?
Am I the only one that CONSISTENTLY has deep problems with this app that makes it almost unusable?
Please someone from Microsoft get in touch with me about this app.
I am a software engineer with more than 12 years of experience and your app is unbelievably awful, and it wasn’t like this 2 years ago. I cannot believe you have allowed this to even be released in this decrepit state.
iPhone 15 here and almost nothing in the app works correctly.
Synchronization constantly has to be done manually after automatic synchronizations that don’t pull everything in, tasks marked in My Day on web and local To-Do instances 70% of the time, synchronization constantly fails to synchronize all subtasks from other To-Do instances web and local >95% of the time, tasks marked in the mobile app don’t always get synchronized, and nothing seems be functionally aligned below the surface with the other platforms app-wise.
Absolutely atrocious quality from a company worth >$1T that has the talent, time, and resources to do better.
So do better.

title: Urgent: Sync no longer works reliable. Please fix ASAP!
body: Since about 10 days the sync of To Do between my devices (MacBook, iPhone, iPad) and between me and people with whom I share lists, does no longer reliably work. The sync happens either with a very long delay or not at all, or only in parts. The issue is fully reproducible and testable. I tested it several times between my devices and with people I share lists with. Other than software updates we did not change any settings. This is a major (!) problem and has already created issues as work when tasks were either not completed, because they did not show on other devices after sync or tasks were done in duplication, because the completion of the tasks were not checked off after sync. This is a major impact on workflows. Microsoft MUSST fix the issue asap. Too many workflows depend on it and it is not easy to establish an alternative quickly.

body:

I have ADHD and I’ve tried literally every to do list or productivity app out there, and this is the only one that has stuck. I’ve tried writing stuff on paper and I always end up losing the paper. In short, this is a life saver!!

title: Lacks basic UX
body:
I’ve tried a mix of similar org app’s, along with paper options. After reading Get Things Done, I was motivated to try again. As an Outlook user this seemed logical.

The Good: so far it’s the best I have found. I’m using it and generally pleased. That’s saying something.

The Bad: very simple UX elements are inconsistent, missing or don’t function as inferred. These are very bad and thus simple (and simply unnecessary). First, starting a new title of a List or Group or Task should always delete the default name in one press of the backspace. In some it does, in others it doesn’t. That’s stupid.

Second, when typing the name of a new Task, List or Group, it should always default to a capitalized first letter. Again, on some it does and others it does not. Once more: stupid.

Lastly, adding a List inside a Group requires an added step. It’s not an easy option. Rather the new List must first be generically added, and then dragged to the intended Group. That’s a PITN and unnecessary. 

Please resolve these simple UX flaws to further improve the app. It’s pretty good but feels rough around the edges as is. I am using the latest version for Apple OS on an iPhone.

title: Very basic todo manager
body:
This is a very basic todo program that is far behind many others on iOS. 

There is no way to create custom smart lists (say based on a tag)

There is no good way to organize a project. Part of the problem is no real subtasks. All you can do is make a checklist in a task. But these items can’t have their own due date, tags etc. so it’s pretty minimal. 

I haven’t found a way to create shared lists. 

No location based reminders. 

My day tasks won’t automatically roll over to the next day if you didn’t complete them (you may not want but it should be an option. )

I guess if you want a task manager that lets you have a pretty background picture this could work for you but unless you need something integrated with your windows pc Microsoft 365 Todo/outlook there’s little reason to use this.

title: App Crashes On iOS devices
body:
I’ve been a long-time user of Microsoft To Do across different platforms, and while it works flawlessly on Android and Windows, the iOS version has become nearly unusable due to a major issue.

After launching the app on my iPhone, it crashes within 1–2 minutes, abruptly closing and returning me to the main menu/home screen. Worse, this crash seems to cause temporary instability in the overall iOS system — other apps freeze or hang briefly, and the device becomes sluggish for a few seconds after the crash. This goes beyond a minor bug and feels like it’s affecting the core performance of iOS itself.

In contrast, the app performs smoothly on Android and Windows, syncing tasks as expected and delivering the productivity support I rely on. The cross-platform experience would be great if not for the iOS-specific issues.

I hope Microsoft addresses this bug soon, as it significantly impacts usability for iPhone users and undermines trust in an otherwise reliable productivity tool.

What I love most is how it actually makes doing daily tasks fun. Checking things off feels rewarding, and the app gives me just enough motivation without feeling like pressure. Whether it’s errands, work goals, or personal habits, this app helps me stay on track and actually enjoy the process.

title: Refuses to sync and crashes
body:
Applications created to help people track their tasks must have only one property which trumps everything else - reliability. As of version 2.140 this app does not have any.
1. It crashes frequently, seemingly when it tries to sync. 
2. Sometimes it doesn't crash but does not sync either. Sync status in the main menu says "Up to Date" but it is not - frequently it shows obsolete state of the tasks which may be a few days old. Attempt to force sync by taping on "Up to Date" does not help.
3. Even when everything  works as designed when you start the app it shows some obsolete state and then after 10-20-30 seconds it refreshes. There is no visual indication if it already refreshed or not so one has to guess. And if you guess wrong you end up editing something which may not even exist anymore.
4. There is no way to submit feedback or debug logs from the app. No way to contact support either. Whom are they hiding from?

To me this app is at the bottom of the ToDo apps pile because of how unreliable and frustrating it is to use every single time.

body: I have 1,300 tasks. This app is terrible for managing a large number of tasks. When using the search field, it searches immediately with each keystroke which bogs down the search process. It also doesn’t allow you to back up one level without re-saving the task, so if you open a task and mistakenly change something the original entry is lost forever unless you force-quit the app and re-open it. Hard to believe that a company like Microsoft could publish such a terrible product.

title: Has so much potential, but falls short
body:
This app could be the best to-do list app on the market, but it needs improvements on simple things.

1) You cannot collapse pictures attached to a task, it simply uses up tons of real estate on the screen with the attached picture.

2) There’s no way to manually sort/prioritize tasks added to the “Important” list.

3) For some reason, manually rearranging tasks in lists that allow it is physically cumbersome. Often times if you don’t place the task just right in the GUI, it will be pulled off the list, sorted elsewhere, or the app will not allow you to move it. Considering rearranging tasks is an integral part of task management, this seriously hinders productivity. It’s annoying at best, and makes the app almost unusable at worst.

4) Unable to assign sub-tasks to “My Day” or “Important” lists. This forces the user to drill down into the list instead of seeing which subtask needs to be accomplished at a glance.

There are other issues, but alas I must actually get things done before heading back to work tomorrow.

title: Great program needs some tweaks
body: A few years back I researched a number of todo programs and used several to test features.  At that time ToDo was Wunderlist, and was my “close second” behind Any.do, which I adopted as my main program, but I still used Wunderlist for grocery lists and other one offs of which I have many (travel checklist, project X etc).  Now that ToDo is integrated with Microsoft office, the situation is much closer, and I would like to actually make the full switch to ToDo.  However, I have found that there are a couple of features on the shared desktop version that are not as functional as for the version that comes on the iPhone app.  Specifically, it is cumbersome to re-order items once they are in the list, as well as to delete them.  It is a snap to do this on the iPhone so I find myself and my admin, with whom I share a couple of ToDo lists, having to enter items on the desktop and then go into the phone to be able to organize them better. title: A decent start
body:
To Do separates out a native Outlook feature into a stand-alone app.

While there are promising features that have started showing up in To Do, it still lacks basic functionality, such as opening an email attached to a task. For business users, this is a must.

Companies that want users to invest in their ecosystems need full integration across their ecosystem… not piecemeal apps that push users out to a browser window constantly.

In order to go from a nice grocery list app to a functional business task manager, To Do still requires a lot of polish, but there’s a promising skeleton underneath.

title: (Update) Still not as good as Wunderlist was and here’s why…
body:
Update from review a few months ago: So another plug - Please add more sort options to the Important list (right under My Day on my screen). It would be absolutely PERFECT if I could sort the Important list by specific lists and in alphabetical order since the grocery lists are set up by store layout. Alternatively, allow users to sort each list with sub-sorts such as: in my TJ’s list, sort by importance, then alphabetically. It should automatically do this, though, IMO. It is simply not functional if trying to use it as a grocery list. If I’ve designed the list by store layout, then I want all the dairy that I’ve starred to be together. 

Why are so many requests being ignored (for years) by Microsoft? I’m about to move on from this app and try another one specifically for groceries, but boy what a headache that would be. To Do could be an excellent, simple app if Microsoft would take care of some key requests (and apparently bugs).

Partial review a few months ago: The “Important” list brings in all the starred tasks, however there still is no option to sort by the different lists each of these starred tasks live in. I have grocery stores as lists and I used to be able to go to the Important list and it would show me all the starred items I needed to purchase, separating it by each grocery store “list”. Worked perfectly! If this sort feature can be added to To Do, I’d seriously consider giving it 5 stars, but not until then.

title: Fills the Gap
body:
Needed: An option to filter the badge count to just items that are overdue. I don’t want to see the count of stuff I have to do today but aren’t due yet.

More: I was a heavy user of Reminders, and that met all my needs until I ran into a performance issue that had me looking for another TODO app. I’ve used Google Tasks and Remember The Milk as well, and those have issues with lack of free badge support, which I depend on. Microsoft To Do filled the gap, providing the performance I needed (so far) as well as the online access and badges for upcoming work. All that said, the badge displays a bloated count, and there’s no option to reduce it to overdue/due work.

Posting this here due to lack of a support contact mechanism for feature requests.

title: If you’re not using this app, you should be
body: I’ve been using To Do for years now, after trying nearly every other competing list app out there. This one isn’t perfect, but it’s pretty darn close. Integrates nigh seamlessly with Outlook. Feature rich. Downright life changing. If you’re still carefully rewriting the unchecked items on your list to a fresh page in a college-ruled spiral notebook (like I did for decades), do yourself a favor and transpose that thing right into To Do. It’ll be in your pocket and at your immediate fingertips from now on.  The ding it makes when you mark a task complete is almost as crossing  off a paper list (and it keeps records of these). Seriously, use this for a few months and you’ll be gushing about it to all your friends and colleagues. You’ll wonder how you ever functioned before. Trust me, you’ll dig it, or your money back (LOL it’s free).

body:

I am a Microsoft 365 business customer so I contacted Microsoft 365 support thinking I could get some help.
 
My support agent did not know what microsoft To Do was. He told me to contact Outlook Mobile support.
 
Outlook Mobile replied to me that they do not maintain To Do and I should contact To Do support. 
 
The To Do help article says in order to contact support, go to my profile and click "Help and Feedback". There is no such button. The closest button is one that leads to a forum where you can post feature ideas that no one at microsoft reads.
 
I suggest that you steer clear of this app, before you become dependent on it and get screwed over by Microsoft.

title: Still the Best Task Manager for Individuals
body:
I am a former Wunderlist user, and I despaired when Microsoft acquired that app and created ToDo.  I thought that the resulting product would be worse.  I was wrong.  I am now happier with ToDo than I ever was with Wunderlist.  ToDo is flexible and powerful such that I can plan my personal, family and work-related projects separately and then cull my daily activities over all tasks / next actions.  ToDo is compatible with GTD.  And it synchronizes over multiple platforms.  When at my workstation, I keep the My Day page open in a window on my righthand screen.  When a new tasks enters my mind, I can immediately enter it on my phone.

I generally don't thank large corporations, but thank you Microsoft for continuing to develop and maintain ToDo.  It has made my life more efficient.

title: MS To Do vs Outlook Tasks
body:
The good:
1. Syncs with Outlook.
2. List (or projects) can be organized in any order. Handy when working with dozens of projects.

The bad:
1. Many Outlook Tasks features missing such as the following:
2. No high, normal, low priority option.
3. No color category option.
4. No recurrence options.
5. Creating a To Do group does not sync over to Outlook Tasks.

I was an Informant 4 user, and it was great! Then, version 5 messed everything up. Looking for a replacement, and Outlook Tasks comes close. However, even though MS To Do syncs with your Outlook Tasks, it does not perform like it. Not very useful without more priority and recurring options.

title: My Tasks for Tomorrow That I Add for My Day Before Tomorrow Gets Deleted
body:
Hi Microsoft. I have an issue with adding my  tasks that are for tomorrow to My Day before tomorrow. title: Not yet ready for prime time
body:
Update:  I dropped Appigo ToDo since writing my original review and now use MS To Do exclusively due to its interoperability with MS Office Tasks. I still won’t increase my rating recommendation because MS has failed to improve features making it a real task manager. In addition to the shortcomings I’ve already mentioned there are bugs they just won’t fix. One such bug is that when completing a task the completion date (as seen in MS Office Tasks) is set to the day BEFORE the actual date. I reported this to MS but they don’t seem to care to fix it. 

For me, MS To Do is just not quite there. I have it installed on my phone and I’m glad to see MS is continuing to add basic features so I’m hoping it will progress to the usefulness I’m looking for. If one is looking for an app to just make check lists it would fine, but if one needs a real task manager it doesn’t do that very well like MS Office Tasks for desktop. Among other features, I want to be able to sort by multiple levels (e.g. due date, then priority, then subject) and similarly to be able to search and sort by categorized completed tasks for archival record keeping. Microsoft, keep improving and I’ll switch when you get there. In the meanwhile, I’ll use an old version of Appigo ToDo which does it all pretty well except they have dropped Syncing with Outlook from newer releases.

title: Missing one feature
body:
This is a great list organizer. Deserves all of the five stars. Having separate lists that can be time organized makes my job, volunteering, and personal life much easier to manage. Now that the planned tasks that fall on the current day automatically populate to the My Day list, it is even more easy to organize. 

I see that the engineers have the capability to create smart lists. The ONLY missing feature I see is the availability for users to organize their own smart lists. i.e. if I have the same word in multiple tasks and I created a keyword list that looked only for that word. I work in residential construction. I have my houses set as different lists. It would be great if I could create a smart/keyword list that looked across all the other lists for tasks that had the word plumber. Then I could have an organized list for everything I had to call the plumber for. Or if I set up inspection dates for separate houses, if some of them feel in the same day a keyword list for inspections would make it easier to organize to make just one call to schedule them.

title: No location based alerts
body:
First of all, Tasks should not be a separate app from Outlook. On every other version of Outlook, tasks are integrated in one app. But on mobile Microsoft makes you bounce back and forth between two apps. Not user friendly. 

Next, I am baffled that Microsoft still cannot figure out how to do location based alerts for Tasks. 

Even Apple and Google have this ability in their weak 1st party task apps. 

But Microsoft still forces you to assign a specific time for every alert. 

So if you want a reminder when you arrive somewhere, or when you leave a location, or when you get in the car, you can’t do it with Outlook tasks. 

So what’s the point of using it at all if I am forced to use a different task app for those?

title: Usable but needs some UI love
body:
The app works fine but the UI design leaves a lot to be desired. For example:

1. New lists items are added to the top rather than being appended to the bottom. Most people think "top down"; we add things in order of importance or anticipated occurrence. The default should be to append to the bottom with the option to prepend.

2. Moving items requires using up/down arrows. On a longer list this is a series of presses and it is easy to accidentally click the wrong item as well. The UI standard has long been a draggable icon on the right side of the list.

3. Sorting by creation date should really be sorting by creation datetime.

4. Editing should have the option for in situ text editing.

title: Great app + Improvements
body:
I use Microsoft To Do regularly to track tasks. It has all the features you would expect for a task tracker - scheduled dates, reminders, recurring tasks, etc. You can also add tasks to “My Day” to make a list of what you want to do today, which is very helpful for me. The app will even give you suggestions what to add to My Day based on scheduled date, which is great. Plus the app syncs with the desktop version in Outlook!

In the past I recommended an improvement to the app, to allow us to skip a recurring task if it was missed. Well, now that feature exists! When you open a task, you can skip to current task if there are past recurrences that you didn’t complete. In Outlook it was already possible to skip a recurring task, so not having that option in the app was a bummer. I’m happy to see that Microsoft is listening to feedback and making improvements to their apps! :)

title: Simple & Functional, Aesthetic
body:
Just what I’ve been looking for. Killing two birds with one app: reminders and todo lists. 

Simple & Functional: 
I am pleased with the fixed categories, very straight forward. 
[Contains: My Day, Important, Assigned to Me, Planned, Tasks].
The fixed categories are divided and separate from the lists you create. 

I appreciate the feature where I can group specific lists if they have similar topics. It makes it much easier to click and find rather than scrolling down and trying to find a certain list in a mountain of lists. 

Aesthetic:
Ability to choose colors or photos as the backdrop of your lists. There’s both dark and pastel versions of certain colors or prepared images you can choose. 

Improvement:
A way to upload new photo backdrops whether from personal photo album or legal website for more variety!! And maybe more colors?

title: Unreliable
body: Unfortunately the notifications for this app are unreliable across all platforms. iOS, Android, macOS and Windows. Apple’s Reminders, Google’s Tasks, TickTick, etc., all give you reliable notifications for recurring tasks, but somehow, and since the app’s initial release, Microsoft just can’t get it right. If you rely on getting notified for whatever reason this app is not for you. It seems that unless the app is open constantly it just forgets to do anything in the background. With time I’ve resigned to using it as a glorified but basic grocery list, but now I’m just switching completely to using another app because why keep 2 apps when I can just use 1 service and be done and know I didn’t miss a thing. Shame because the app’s features, design and layout are great. But what’s the point if it just doesn’t work?

The features for prioritization (minimal, silly) and tagging are non-existent... I could go on and on, but u get the point that this is a 3, at best, that candidly could be much more... The UI is also built to child-like user expectations, rather than for people who want function and detail, from their perspective (how to slice and dice their ability to do task management with filters for information, for instance, not homogenized UI’s with no sophistication… this is a kiddie task app… ONE level of tasks and then useless step structure.

title: No calendar integration, can slide to rearrange in all areas and more.  Needs work
body:
App needs some functionality added and some changes made! Disappointing without the following: 
 1. Calendar integration with holidays and birthdays. A monthly calendar view would be nice too. 
 2. Ability to slide up and down in all areas to rearrange items (allows it in some places, not in others= super annoying)
3. Ability to add multi-day planned items. 
 4. Ability to add time ranges to planned items or tasks. For ex. 7:30-9:30, not just a static time ex. 7:30. 
 5. Seeing issues with items on same day not sorting by time. Tasks should auto arrange based on time of day. For example 10am item shouldn’t show up before the 7am item.
6.  Let us share our planned and task smart item lists with other users like we can with other lists.   For example my wife and I use this app.   I can’t share any planned items or task with her, it’s foolish to not have that ability.

title: Simple and effective
body:
I don’t normally leave reviews but hopefully this can help someone like me, who has trouble staying organized and planning things if they aren’t written down. I much prefer pen and paper, but in today’s digital age it’s not realistic to always have both on hand and easily accessible.

First of all, I’ve tried so many different task apps over the years (both paid and free) and I’m so happy to have finally settled on this one. 

The interface is very simple; you just type and press enter and your task is set. Additionally, you may opt to set reminders and due dates, either at time of writing or later. My favorite feature is the Siri compatibility, so I can always add things even if I can’t type at that moment.

Next, this app wins because I no longer have to browse through a bunch of different lists and categories to see what needs to be done urgently; I can see exactly what needs to be done today, next week, and next month. I can also see what doesn’t have a due date, and one can be assigned later. The ability to sort by lists and urgency simultaneously is phenomenal.

Finally, I only use Apple products and this syncs flawlessly across my iPhone, iPad, iWatch, and MacBook. Overall, this app does wonders for my productivity. Keep it simple!

title: It’s ok, since it’s free, but not MS quality
body:
There’s no indefinite reminder function, that is, a reminder without a deadline date and the push notification only functions once. If you’re using the app to remind yourself to take, say, medication indefinitely, then you’ll only get a push notification once and there’s no option to remind you without a due date; it’s annoying to scroll through the months shown in their in-built calendar to set a date far into the future to get a reminder that only works in the app (don’t remember to open their app, then you won’t get notified of your reminder, except for one time). Apple’s reminder app lets you do both: recurring push notifications and no definite deadline. It seems the developers hard coded a lot of the deadline reminder options when setting a reminder instead of giving the user more choice and freedom to set deadlines like they want easily or to not set deadlines at all and still get a frequent push notification reminder.

I find the various lists confusing, starred list, my day list, smart list, etc. Hard to keep track of it all. Basically, all the various lists increase the complexity of using this app, making it hard to remember where you put a specific task. So, it’s best to limit the lists you use. I only bother with the starred list and lists I make myself.

The app also blocks off your text at the bottom of a note in the new task creation/edit menu when you make a long note, so editing a note after a new task is created is impossible unless you delete a lot of the text that is visible in the note. Basically, you need to keep your notes super short if you use that feature, since you don’t know where the text cutoff for visibility is when editing a note. If you don’t edit a note after creation, then it’s not a problem to see the entire note.

Other than the issues I mentioned, the app works well. It has never crashed on me, yet. It seems to backup tasks automatically, but I don’t know if that feature actually works.

title: A perfect digital brain
body:
This is BY FAR my absolute FAVORITE app ever. This app is a direct extension of my brain. It keeps all my thoughts organized. It is a perfect holding place for all the crazy ideas and things I need to get done that pop up in my brain. I can easily dump them here and then focus on what I need to. I’ve been using this for years back when it was Wunderlist.

I can’t say enough good things about it. Best app ever. This keeps my personal to do list, my business to do list, my wish list, shopping list, books I want to read (but won’t ever get around to actually reading), business ideas, writing ideas, silly crazy ideas, movies I want to see, my vehicle maintenance schedules, my goals, my dreams and everything in between. 

As a side note I also use a simple but crazy-effective emoji system. I put an emoji in front of each to-do item. For example the hammer emoji means fix, a tree means outdoor project, a squid emoji means organization project, thread=sewing, car=car, computer=computer, etc. after that I put a number emoji which means how long I think that project will take. The app allows you to sort alphabetically so all the emojis are all grouped. When I have time, all I do is look at my to-do list and decide what kind of project I’m going to tackle and how much time I have. Then I get things done. Yes I was that really productive friend when the pandemic hit and we all got laid off. I was crushing it, getting things done, building stuff, starting side businesses. All with the help of Microsoft To-Do.

title: Not ready for prime time, far from it
body:
The primary fault I have with this app is the lack of ability to schedule tasks. It allows you to assign a due date and will let you set a reminder, but true scheduling of a task is wholly missing. 

What I mean is that I want to be able that a task is due to be complete by a certain time on a certain date. And then the list of tasks is presented in that order. Here’s what I need to do first today, then what I need to do next, etc. items with a due date but no required due time would be at the end of the list for that day. The reminder field in the app would be used more for telling me when to start a task. 

A secondary fault is a more robust prioritization. More than just a star or not star rating, it needs to let me say that a task has a high, medium, or low priority. That way, if I have to let a task slip, I’ll know which one. The “Errands” app does this well. I don’t use it because I need a to-do app that will work both on my iPhone and my PC. 

Next, categorization would be very nice. Thus, I can assign a task to a “Field” category or an “Office” category, depending on where it needs to be done. Then I could filter on the “Field” tasks when I head out the door. This should be a free-form data field so I can make up my own list of categories. But it should be such that I can see all tasks if I want to, not just one category. 

Finally, integration with Outlook on my PC would be great.

Update 3/24/21: I started using To-Do again after a hiatus of several months using the “AnyDay” app on my iPhone and iPad. That app is iOS-only and I really needed an app that was integrated with Win10. So, back to “To-Do”. 

My impressions above came back to me in spades. Sorting ability is essentially non-existent. The To-Do app is an amateurish effort by a company with vast software development capability. If I were Microsoft, I would be ashamed of this app.

title: “Completed” volume is tied to ringer volume
body:
iOS has two volume sliders: in-app volume (for games or media for example) and the ringer volume.  When checking off completed items, a ding is played back at the ringer volume and not at the app volume.  In, for example, a grocery store, this noise is loud and draws attention and it is not easy to turn it down because the ringer volume is set in settings.  

Turning the ringer down for an app and then needing to turn it back up to hear when you are called, is not a great experience. 

Background notes: Recently my ringer volume setting was changed so that I have to go into settings to change it. (This might be a new default system setting, there is a setting to turn it back. )  It also makes sense to keep the ringer at a useful volume while reducing the chance of accidentally leaving it quiet.  This may be the way Apple is moving going forward.

title: So close to perfect! Needs location awareness/geofencing
body:
The way this functions and performs has the robustness, flexibility, dependability and platform-agnosticism to be a reliable personal task manager. It provides enough structure so one doesn’t need to think too much about where things go, yet isn’t too rigid where you feel like you need to work around limitations/restrictions. Works the same across all devices. Has rich-enough detail to use as a quick notes inbox w/ photo and file attachment included. Easy to add subtasks. Has alert and due dates as separate fields for fine tuned notifications.

The only thing that needs to be added is geofence-based notifications so one can schedule alerts to be triggered when leaving or reaching a designated location. It would be great if this could also be combined with the alert times too, so you could schedule an notification for when you leave work only after 5:00pm. This feature is available in Apple reminders, and that comes really close to To Do minus the native app availability on other platforms.

Microsoft, if you’re reading this, y’all have made the ultimate free task management app, and it has significantly improved my life. If you can add the geolocation features that would make this app perfect!

title: Unintuitive set up. List sorting process totally flawed.
body:
I really liked the Wunderlist app. Literally no complaints. I was very sad when it was retired. With To Do, however,I have many issues. I have actually never written an app review, because I’m usually pretty laid back with this kind of thing. But there are enough idiotic things about this app that made me want to review it. 

The issue I find THE most frustrating about this app is the “sort” feature. You can only sort items with lists according to: importance, alphabetically, due date, and creation date. There is no inherent sorting WITHIN those categories, which is seriously flawed. I should be able to sort an entire list by importance (having all of those starred items move to the top of the list) and then ALSO have those items organized by due date or another way. That way I could look at my important tasks, and instead of seeing a jumble of due dates, they would be organized chronologically. It just makes no sense to me that one categorization automatically and completely means that all other categories are excluded from use. Why?! 

Also, if the sorting tool is really going to be that inept and handicapping, then at least there should be an option to sort manually between items, shifting them up and down as you’d like. But there is not. 

Lastly, when you sort by due date, the first due date to show up on your list is whatever is due the next day.... NOT whatever items you have marked as added to “my day.”  How on earth does that make sense? “My day” items should automatically be at the top of the list, followed by tomorrow’s items. 

All in all, I’m disappointed in this app. There is very little about it that is intuitive (and what is, is just a mimicry of Wunderlist). And the organizational options are nonsensical at best. It seems like it was designed by people who have actually never used it in real life or have very disorganized minds.

MS bought Wunderlist then evidently executed all the developers for treason to the Microsoft credo of bloated, inefficient programming.  Just basic stuff is missing here. Add a new task from the main menu? Tough, you can only create new lists and groups. Want to search within a list? Tough again, you can only search from the main menu. It seems trivial but you end up switching back and forth dozens of times because some genius decided to keep the "new task" function and "search for a task" function on separate pages. If you want to just see your inbox every time you open To Do, your out of luck and will be presented with "Insights" -- which, in a surprise to no one, are not very insightful. 

Good luck leaving feedback for developers within the app, where you have to created a separate account, go through a dozen steps and then send in your remarks via carrier pigeon.

body: I would give zero stars if I could. I used to love Wunderlist, it made coordinating shopping/packing/to do lists with my easy and fast. Lists updated between users and stayed in sync. Ever since wunderlist was phased out and Microsoft To Do has replaced it we have had nothing but issues. Inviting people to lists sometimes works, even if they accept the invite the app might not add them to the list. On shared lists, the app doesn't stay updated. Even if I force it to sync, my lists won’t stay updated. This makes shopping very difficult if my wife adds an item, but I miss it because my list hasn’t synced. Even when I check items off, they don’t remove from other peoples lists. I’ve tried logging out and back in, deleting and reinstalling the app. Nothing has helped.

title: A nice start but a long way to go
body:
I’ve read other reviews giving kudos to Microsoft for finally updating the Todo feature list to equal Wunderlist. That very well may be true, but I dumped Wunderlist years ago in favor of other apps with better features and fewer bugs. In my opinion, Microsoft Todo is still years behind other apps in terms of basic usability. Adding a repeating task is insanely clunky, task groups are inexplicably and randomly duplicated for no reason, and importing tasks from other apps is virtually impossible (for example, importing an email as a task creates an entry with the entire body of the email as the task name. Why not just the subject line guys?). 

There is no integration with iOS at all. Want to import Reminders? Can’t do it. Want to see basic calendar information on your My Day view? Can’t do it. Want to add a widget to your home screen like every other freakin’ app ever developed? Can’t do it. 

Also, the flagged emails feature is a joke. Reading the Microsoft website, this feature only works for emails sent to an “account hosted by Microsoft, such as an Outlook.com, Hotmail.com, or Live.com account.” Business users may be in luck since accounts hosted by Microsoft but with a custom domain are also included. Gmail users are out of luck. Yahoo? Out of luck. I can’t even remember the last time I received an email from a Hotmail or Outlook user that wasn’t sent immediately to spam. 

Speaking of Outlook, you can’t create a Todo task directly from an email in Outlook because Outlook doesn’t support that. 

Things, Todoist, and other competing apps are YEARS ahead of Microsoft Todo. Apple is even catching up quickly with the built in Reminders app.

title: Not great, not very collaborative
body:
Updated a few months later: rating has gone down. This app keeps getting worse and worse. I also was recently logged out and for god knows what reason, Microsoft doesn’t recognize my user info so I can’t get in, and my lists are gone forever. Even when I used to be able to access, things wouldn’t move cleanly, and would too easily nest within another item rather than move next to that item (it’s a lot like what happens on Outlook on my work account, but that’s a different story). It’s also not possible to use this list on an encrypted computer and have it synch with a phone app (per customer support a few months ago) which makes it impossible to do any updating from my work computer. I seriously didn’t think I could hate this app any more than I did when it first came out, but here we are.......

Just had to get this because for some reason Wunderlist is being discontinued. There are too many mandated lists (my day and tasks) that I can’t remove even though I won’t use them. I dislike not being able to change the main page from a plain and bleak white, and that customization only happens within individual lists. But most importantly, it’s proving to be hugely challenging to share lists with my partner, which is the main reason we use lists. It’s not proving functional to text our links to each other (Android vs iPhone) and neither of us actually wants a Microsoft account so email sharing is proving challenging too. We’re also trying to share lists with his family as we are caregivers for them and it is not easy for them to gain access to. Super disappointed in a simple shared list app being monopolized and losing quality and function.

title: Game Changer
body: This app is extremely useful and, unlike many apps that are merely fun and interesting, this one could literally change your life or business if applied thoughtfully.  It has some features built in which seem to follow suggestions from mainstream best sellers on organization such as one of my personal favorites: Getting Things Done by David Allen.  I know it is based off another program which I never owned.  I use the app on my iPhone, iPad and two versions on my desktop—one in a web browser and an iOS app.  All four versions have similar features but actually have some extra features you gave to search for almost like a treasure hunt!  The browser version allows you to copy tasks and next steps which allows you to create templates for repeated tasks.  You can share lists with friends/co-workers as well to delegate next-steps.  I recommend you explore the program thoroughly before spending time making detailed lists—there are a few things it cannot do, and knowing what they are helps you to organize your lists properly.  I am still exploring the program but have been using it with a lot of success.  Good luck.  I’m sure Microsoft will continue to improve the program over time.

title: Tasks and Outlook
body:
Hello - I love tasks, however it doesn’t community to email as I would like. It doesn’t allow me to create a note/task tied directly to an email. Every email that comes in has action items tied to it. So if we had the ability to add a Note/task to that email, it would help us focus on the actionable items of importance. If we open 100 emails a day, that’s a lot of action items. And if we wanted to prioritize those actions of importance, we need an organized way to see those actions. So the tasks would appear in 2 locations exactly the same. Duplicate. One on the task bar as it is today, and the other would appear as a icon of some sort on the email itself. Could you add an icon on the email options for “tasks/notes” with time and date stamps on them so we can get even more strategic on what we are completing first. 

Also, if we do get the option to create an action task for email, can that option also be made available for the mobile app. I try and work on my phone as often as I can however it’s not as efficient as the desktop applications.

title: Looking for a way out
body:
We manage our grocery list collaboratively. I used wunderline to repopulate the list when I reorganized it. I also keep cooking notes and recipes in ToDo. And have another ~90 lists that were imported from Wunderlist. 

ToDo doesn’t have import except from Wunderlist, but the wunderline server is dead. 
ToDo doesn’t have search/replace.
ToDo doesn’t have a print dialogue/capability. 
Search is a nightmare, as it searches all lists. We are out of salt. I need to star “salt” on the grocery list. Searching for salt gets me pages and pages of recipes that include salt. It’s easier to scroll through a 700-item grocery list than search for a simple string. 

I feel betrayed. 

I managed to export a JSON file and will hack that or use it as a template if I can figure out how to reimport the manipulated content. 

Save yourself a major headache and look elsewhere for task management apps.

title: Features are fine but so laggy I frequently give up
body:
UPDATE: Since my original review on June 18, things have gotten worse with the performance on the iPad mini. Now the app hangs and then shuts down before it ever opens on my iPad mini 4. It works “OK” on my iPhone. On a positive note I really like the concept behind the My Day list. I like that it forces you to reassess the things that need to be done each day instead of dragging along all the things that didn’t get accomplished the day before. It would be nice if the planned/scheduled items for each day auto-populated but I can live without that. Also, I t would be nice if the app could be synced with or at least shared with Google calendar. As far as I can tell there is no direct way to do that.

A couple of months ago I dutifully migrated my data from Wunderlist, which I lived by, to To Do. I was prepared to be disappointed, but hopeful that there had truly been integration between the two apps. So far I have found the UI with To Do to be easy to use and I’m navigating subtle changes to organize my days and lists. In this arena I’m pretty happy and there are some things that work even better than Wunderlist. 
Where I am NOT happy is the performance of the app on iOS. I use my iPad Mini 4 for most everything, and almost without fail I am stopped in my tracks by lag every time I use To Do. Half the time I end up abandoning whatever list I’m trying to create because I get so frustrated. If I restart the app it takes forever to reload. My iOS gets updated regularly so I don’t think that’s an issue. I’m more concerned that it’s a Microsoft/Apple compatibility issue, and if so, that would be very disheartening. I never had problems with Wunderlist doing this until Microsoft took it over, but once that happened Wunderlist was laggy too. I really hope this can get worked out. I’d like to be able to continue using To Do
The other issue I have is that I am not allowed to share my personal To Do lists with coworkers on their work Outlook. I had my personal Microsoft account before we had Outlook accounts for work and all my To Do lists are on my personal account. If I can’t share with others from my personal account is there any easy way for me to migrate my personal to do lists to my work Outlook account without copying them all over? Thank you.

title: Let’s Buy An App And Make It Slightly Worse

I just don’t get it. If you wanted to buy a popular to do list app so you can have a preexisting user base to mine data from, fine, but don’t change the functionality or design of the app! Just call it Microsoft’s Wunderlist. Frustrating. But thanks for leaving scraps of the original app’s functionality behind. 

I love what you guys have done with opening the Windows platform up and providing Office on iPhone and Android, Microsoft is now one of the more progressive tech companies thanks to Nadella but the decision to mess with success with regards to this app was a misguided one.

title: Wunderlist was Superior
body:
I really cannot stand this app, but I use it because they hijacked Wunderlist and then tossed it in the trash, forcing us into this mess. Yes, it looks very similar to Wunderlist, and they gave a half-*** attempt and making it work like Wunderlist, but it fails in so many areas. 

I feel it’s temperamental. For example, when I’m trying to move an item, it’s is to difficult make sure it goes in between other list items. It’s instead VERY easy to accidentally drop a list item onto another item, forcing that item to become a sub-item under another item, which appears that said action cannot be undone 😳! So we have to delete the sub-item and manually add it back onto the list by creating it a new list item again. This is a huge problem when it comes to my time and productivity. 

The other pretty annoying issue is my completed items populate in my not-completed item list. This may be fine for some tasks, but most certainly is not for a perpetual grocery list. There should be an option on how we’d like to view the completed items. I loved how Wunderlist kept completed tasks at the very bottom so when I needed to view them, I could scroll through ONLY completed items. Now I have to wait for THOUSANDS of completed grocery items that have been purchased over the years to populate (because I imported my Wunderlist). Another huge bog-down in terms of my time and productivity. 

There’s a few other annoyances but
These are the ones that I need fixed to ever be content with Microsoft’s version of Wunderlist.

title: Just ok
body:

Planned list used to give tabs of earlier, today, tomorrow, the three days following, and later  - which worked for me, but not others. Now it sorts each day, individually, for about two weeks out and hides the older (missed) stuff after a few days. Instead of replacing the sort order, why not add? 

With the two above issues combined, I have *too much* information about what’s coming up on my lists and absolutely no (good) way to reduce it down to a manageable amount. 

Additionally, I can no longer hide deleted items on some of my lists, making my shopping list annoying. I’m hoping this snuck in accidentally and is not a new “feature.”

Finally, there’s an ongoing bug that will randomly add an additional day to repeating tasks. For example, if I have things repeating every Monday, it’ll show up as due every Monday and Tuesday. If I repeat every 7 days, however, this doesn’t happen, so there’s a workaround, but it needs to be fixed.

title: FINALLY Matches & Surpasses Wunderlist!
body: This morning, the creators of “Microsoft To Do” FINALLY fixed enough of the features on this app to meet my former expectations of “Wunderlist!” “Microsoft To Do” (at first) had a lot of fun new features like colorful backgrounds for lists, and a few more sorting options, but was still missing some of the BASICS I enjoyed in “Wunderlist:” Here are my favorite two: 1) Being able to quickly recover a RECENTLY checked-off item at the TOP of the completed items, within a given list. Example: In “To Do” completed items were initially only alphabetized. I have an ongoing (reusable) grocery list including HUNDREDS of products. I even number them, by aisle, to ensure I see them “in order.” (Even if I’m in a different store, it still, at least, “categorizes” them together). But an “accidentally checked off” item, while shopping, was virtually GONE (until I got home & realized what was missing). This was fixed! Now I can just look at the TOP of the completed list. And, 2) Now I can see upcoming tasks separated out BY DAYS. In the past, anything beyond tomorrow was lumped together. Now, just like in Wunderlist, I can quickly find an upcoming day to which a task can be quickly moved/reassigned. And one of my favorite NEWER features of “To Do:” if you want certain tasks to recur/repeat in the future, say, only Mondays Wednesdays & Fridays (as opposed to once a week, or once a day) it can do this! Very cool. Keep up the great work!

title: Best To-Do minder for today's tasks
body:
Easy to use, with all of the features you need to get today's tasks in front of you.

I use multiple to-do apps. Some are great for complex projects (although MS To-Do allows for multiple steps), some are better for sharing, like grocery lists. But none are as good as MS To-Do for daily, decide the day's priorities and work that list. 

You can add tasks easily to a general pile or a group or directly to My Day. Then drag-and-drop tasks into My Day. Work the list, check off completed items, and My Day is cleared each day forcing you to reconsider what you will work on the next day. 

Within a Group easily move tasks up and down to reflect your priorities. And I use the Stars on a task to give me an easy reminder as to which tasks I want to move back to My Day if I didn't complete the day before. But you can also use the Lightbulb on My Day to bring up yesterday's uncompleted tasks and recently added tasks.

title: NOT designed around the user anymore
body:
Microsoft take over of Wunderlist feels binary. 
It seems to be designed under the assumption that once a task is complete, it is complete for eternity. This strikes me as a male – engineer mindset.
This ignores the probable scenario and common use case of reusable lists.
For example, workouts, grocery shopping, house cleaning, gardening, inventory management, homeschooling, weekly work routines, etc. These activities can involve long “completed“ lists. If you can’t sort those completed lists, they become unwieldy. Basically, they become useless. 

I used to be able to go through my completed lists and turn them back into active to do‘s. Now it’s just too much trouble. If I want to alphabetize a completed list, I have to take 20 minutes to uncheck every item on the completed list to add it back to the uncompleted list, and then run an alphabetize function, and then remember everything that was already done and headed back to the completed list, in reverse alphabetical order.It’s an absurd process you are forcing users to follow in order to make a list reusable. author: ElectraSF

title: Merely populates iPhone Reminders
body: I’ll give this app 2-stars because it doesn’t crash ... but seriously, why would anyone WANT to quit using the superior Wunderlist for this half-effort?  Any item you create is stored in the iPhone Reminders as a to-do, but neither scheduled nor shared with associates. Items are not entered by default with a due date, and even if you do add a due or reminder date, they’ll disappear from “today” and don’t carry over to tomorrow, so you must manually add any tasks from a single list of ALL tasks. If you mark an item with a star ... well that’s meaningless. And should you open your iPhone Reminders, you’ll find 100’s of stored there, thereby making simple reminders (like “go to bed”) lost amongst the work tasks that didn’t require being spammed through the Reminders app, not to mention now your to-do of “turn in report” has the same unimportant notification appearance, sound, and limited snooze options as “pick up kids from school”. Utterly worthless and a lesson for how to drive away millions of customers so an app exists solely to have O365 but without any of Wunderlist’s functionality. What a waste.

author: Bhunkii

title: It’s lacking a very important feature
body:
I used our beloved Wunderlist up until the end. And that’s because it had all the best features. I can’t tell you how many apps I’ve downloaded to try and replace Wunderlist, but none of them measured up. They’ve all been deleted. I’m keeping To-Do because I’ve got a little glimmer of hope that they’ll add the one feature that’s keeping me from loving it. 

I used Wunderlist for everything: work, personal life. My favorite was having a “permanent” grocery list of all our usual items. I only starred what I wanted, un-starring when the item was picked up, repeat process. It took the stress out of shopping. In Wunderlist, you can click on the “starred” tab and all the items are beautifully categorized, making shopping a breeze. The whole grocery list was broken down in a way that made sense. 

My ONLY gripe with To-Do is that the starred items aren’t categorized! They’re all jumbled, it’s a total mess and it’s nearly impossible for me to shop the way I used to. Now I to use it to check off items I want, and then I have to write everything down on a piece of paper (for shame) so that I can see it all broken down by category. 

PLEASE allow the starred items to be separated out by category like they were so beautifully in Wunderlist!

title: How Can You Work for 3+ Years to Create A Far Worse App?
body:
See all of the comments here of users bemoaning the loss of Wunderlist.  The developers then respond “please let us know which features you miss.”  It has been years since the purchase of Wunderlist, you would think that they would have taken Wunderlist’s great aesthetic and feature set and advanced them forward. You would unfortunately be wrong.

(This is from Microsoft, the company that normally crams additional features into their software and is concerned that no feature ever gets dropped. )

Anyway, features I miss:
— No quick entry panel on the Mac. See Wunderlist, Todoist, Things, OmniFocus.
—No actual linkage between iOS or Mac Outlook and Todo. See See Wunderlist, Todoist, Things, OmniFocus.
—No linkage to Mac Mail.
—No calendar linkage or support. See Todoist, Things, OmniFocus.
—Nice background colors. Beyond the photo of Berlin, Wunderlist’s backgrounds were nicer. Why can’t we insert our own? Why are there so few?
—No support for Siri Shortcuts. See Wunderlist, Todoist, Things, OmniFocus. What exactly have you been “developing”?
— No Apple Watch app. Microsoft doesn’t have enough developers????  There are companies with One developer that have managed this. 

Overall, I have been a real fan of Microsoft’s development since Satya took over the helm.  But, given the huge head start from the Wunderlist base, and the developer capability of Microsoft, it’s hard to imagine how they could have done this more poorly.  This is a very competitive space—if Todo were really “Wunderlist on Steroids” they wouldn’t be forcing Wunderlist customers off the platform, they would have jumped already with no coaxing.

title: Don’t normally write reviews.
body:
Anybody migrating from Wunderlist will not be happy with this app as it currently stands. It will require updates to include features you previously used and relied on. Until those features are included, you might need to look elsewhere.

Wunderlist was a fantastic app with incredibly intuitive features that greatly improved efficiency. When you have a great app, why change it? Overall this is a shell of the Wunderlist app and is missing the key features that made the app so powerful and user friendly.

Missing calendar feed: this was probably my favorite feature as it allowed me to see my upcoming tasks in my iCalendar.

Missing smart scheduling feature: in Wunderlist you could type in the task line: “Submit paper April 31 11:59pm” and it would automatically insert the due date and time. Less things to click and scroll through aka more efficient. Migrating from Wunderlist, I expected at the very least a poorly designed smart scheduling feature.

Additionally, My Day should automatically transfer over things that are due today. That would seem pretty logical to me. It makes me feel like there’s some disconnect and I become uneasy about possibly forgetting something which is the opposite of the feeling I should be getting while using this app.

If I wasn’t somebody who had used Wunderlist daily for 5 years, my review might be more favorable. This app has incredible potential to become #1 on the App Store productivity category, but the developers are going to need to listen to the team that developed Wunderlist and it’s migrating users.

Wunderlist was great! Microsoft takes over and it turns to rubbish!!

Do not download this app if you actually want to keep track of things that need to be done!!!

title: Buggy still
body:
A great start and I’m happy so far. I used to be an avid user of Astrid and Wunderlist, and have been pretty frustrated these good apps keep getting bought by mega corporations. (Yahoo and Microsoft)

For this app, there are some bugs and quirky behaviors that are frustrating. I migrated from Wunderlist and these weren’t issues before. Some example below:

- The weekly recurring tasks don’t work. Just try it. If I set it for Friday, it somehow labels it as “Thu, Fri”. Is it a time zone issue? I’m in ET.
- The sorting doesn’t work well. As we could in Wunderlist or even Excel, a sort order should not lock the list. We should still be able to move items around. Imagine a use case, where I want the list to be first sorted by items in the order they were created...then I want to reorder some items to appear on top.  Not possible right now. We just end up having a jumbled mess. 
- When you inadvertently check off an item, it’s almost impossible to find it to uncheck it if you had Completed Items hidden. In Wunderlist, when a task is completed, it gets sent to the bottom and they are sorted in the order which they were completed. Now not anymore. It’s jumbled elsewhere and due to the weird sorting behavior (mentioned above), I can’t find it. 
- No easy way to purge completed items? This should be a setting. I had hundreds maybe thousands in some lists, and I had to manually delete each one. (I had to because I felt the app was slow.)

title: Bleh
body:
I was a Wunderlist user and I used it for very simple things - groceries, personal to-do’s, etc. Light, simple use. Loved Wunderlist. I’ve experienced Issues with this app that seem very basic to me, though. For example:
- Synching is buggy. I share several lists with my wife and somehow we end up with lists that aren’t exactly the same sometimes. Just got home from the grocery store, wife’s list has hamburger buns, mine didn’t. Watched as we synched again and still not on my list. Of course additional trips to the grocery store are now not so routine.
- when I toggle the app to show items crossed off a list, that works. When I toggle back to not showing them it freezes. Every. Single. Time.
- it won’t let me move something to the very bottom of the list. Have to move it to second to last, then move the last item up one.
- seems very easy to inadvertently cross something off when scrolling compared to Wunderlist.
- the nesting feature seems nice in concept, but it’s very easy to accidentally nest something under another to-do item when moving things around on an iPhone, and for the life of me I can’t figure out how to un-nest it. So, stuck with deleting it and adding it again.

I would expect some bugs from a fairly new app but seems like Microsoft should be able to do better than the average little app builder. So, we’re gonna use Wunderlist until we can’t then find something else.

Original Review:

title: Ugh
body:
I’m actually near tears trying to use this replacement app. There are so many things that are intolerable, some of which I’ve read about, so I’ll just list the few that are most egregious:

1. Themes: if the themes that were available in Wunderlist were just brought over, this transition wouldn’t feel like a bandaid was just ripped off. But instead, just a few Microsoft-style colors and Microsoft-style pictures are available, and must be chosen by screen. The visual of the theme in Wunderlist was a huge part of its simplicity, especially since it could be made dark. 

2. Manual population of My Day — every day — is maddening. You actually have to think about what should be placed there which completely defeats the purpose of an electronic To Do list. I could just use paper, which I’m actually considering. 

3. My name at the top is a complete waste of space and a distraction. I already know my name. 

Hopefully Wunderlist will still be operational after May, even if it doesn’t sync, because that’s where I’m staying until I can’t anymore.

title: Can be frustrating to use
body:
I used Wunderlist to keep running meal plans and a grocery list. I switched over to To Do when they emailed us about phasing out the app. Since using to do, I have been annoyed with the “show completed tasks” feature. It’s easy to accidentally check off an item that you haven’t completed. In Wunderlist, I could quickly figure out what I clicked by accident, because it kept the crossed off item in the same location in the list (showed it in it’s original location with the uncompleted tasks still there). In to do, if you say to show completed tasks, it pulls them up in a totally different order... like a running list of completed to do’s. There is no way for me to figure out which one I just removed from my list by mistake. 

My app is also freezing up when I say “hide completed tasks”. It won’t go back to my list. I have to shut the app down and reopen it. 

When scrolling sometimes the app thinks I’ve selected a task and moves it... I understand the desire to rearrange items, but I would rather that be a separate menu or something. I make my grocery list in an order to begin with. I don’t want that order changed because I’m scrolling. Maybe include an edit option that allows you to move items, but make items stay put unless you specifically tap the dot to check them off. 

Too much happens by accident!

title: Wunderlist was MUCH better
body:

THINGS I LOVED IN WUNDERLIST:

Also, it used to send finished items to the bottom under a completed listing. This meant I could easily find completed items if I accidentally erased them or wanted to recheck what IHad done. The ToDo app just leaves them mixed in with everything current.
Wunderlist added new items to the top of the list...To Do adds them to the bottom. I much preferred adding to the top.
I could print Wunderlist...can’t find a way to do this in To Do.
These are a few of the reasons I feel To Do is a giant step backwards from Wunderlist.
I hope they add these features soon, or I’ll have to try and find something better.

title: Wunderlist Pros/Cons
body:
PROS:

— Microsoft uses Wunderlist’s simple user interface. Great!

— Importing non-shared lists from Wunderlist was straightforward although a bit slow.

CONS:

— Recreating shared lists from Wunderlist is dreadful. This is because each person must install the ToDo app and import all of his or her private lists for their devices and accounts. But the import process creates a private list on each person’s devices for each shared list. Getting back to a single shared list requires everyone to delete the imported private list having the name of the shared list to allow the owner to re-share his or her original imported list.  This was tedious with just two-person sharing. I can’t imagine the difficulty in setting up your devices if lists are shared with multiple persons having different owners.

— By default, lists are imported with completed tasks showing. Hiding a long list of completed task takes forever, and locks up the app while it is being done.

— There is no way to determine if a shared list is in sync with other users. You have to dig to find the mechanism to manually sync a list. Even after doing a manually sync, my shared grocery list does not contain the latest item that my spouse added to the list. (I’ve been waiting 30 minutes.) I can’t imagine using MicroSoft ToDo for a joint shopping trip to the grocery store. This is something my spouse and I did often with Wunderlist to split up the shopping effort while both of us were in the same store. I’ve contacted support in this regard, and will update this review with a response (if I receive one.)

I will update this review as I find other issues. Good luck!

title: Transitioning is a little painful
body:
I’m transitioning off Wunderlist and am giving MS to do a try. The import was very quick and easy so I appreciate that. The app itself is similar although there are some key issues that are causing very big annoyances with daily use. 

Overall, this is a great app that is FREE. We’re so used to getting all these from Wunderlist that sometimes we don’t take the time to appreciate the work that is done and offered for free.  Thank you. 

The items below are a few area where the app can be improved. 

Accidental actions. I’ve noticed that I’ve been accidentally marking things a lot while trying to scroll. I started comparing the two apps and noticed that Wunderlist was superb at this.  

In Wunderlist the whole horizontal space was scrollable, include the checkbox and the star. This made scrolling extremely easy and prevented any accidental marking tasks. Only when you really narrowed in and wanted to mark something, did it actually mark the task. 

In To Do, The vertical scrolling is limited to the text in the middle and not to the checkbox or the star on the edges. Because of this, when you try to scroll near the left or right edge, you end up accidentally marking something completed or important. This seems to be happening a lot.. at least for me (could be user error)... the actions seem a little too sensitive. 

When you accidentally mark something complete, there is no undo and therefore you must go to show “completed items”, search for it and uncheck the item.  This has become very cumbersome. 

Also, Another review mentioned it, but the “planned” section (previously) “Week” has become rather clutter. I see the idea they are going for, however, this section works better as a high level view of your week instead cluttering it with too much information, grouped in an impractical way.  When you get to Saturday or Sunday, the next week is clumped into one section and that is not helpful. 

The idea is nice but I don’t see if being as useful as a simple week view separated by days. It would be great to at least show the next 5 days (or however many) split out. 

Thank you and keep up the great work.

title: A Lesser Wunderlist
body:
The app has potential, but the “My Day” feature should not be a forced feature.  

I prefer the “Today” menu in Wunderlist, which was sectioned by project and was easy to control.  It was so simple that Wunderlist became my note taking tool anytime I need to quickly jot something down.  I didn’t have to worry about the note getting lost deep in the tasks, since it appeared as one of the today’s tasks.  From there, once again, it was easy to control.

The “My Day” feature poses as a decluttering tool, but is really a redundancy that forces there to be two due dates to a task instead of one.  “Today” was same as “My Day”, except you mark whatever you will not be able to do today vs. marking what you will be able to do today.  At the very least, we should have both options.

This app beats Wunderlist in the sync feature, notes functionality, app crashes, and design.  But, the fundamentals are lackluster for a Microsoft product.  Users being forced off Wunderlist to this is unfortunate.

The earlier tab brings up tasks I’ve not set dates for and ironically haven’t used recently but the only way I can remove them is by marking them as complete and 100% eliminating them. So unless I want to continuously create a new  shopping task rather than edit the preexisting one in my earlier tab I guess they’ll have to hang around uselessly in Planned. The other issue I have with Planned is how jumbled up the rest of the week looks when you’re trying to see what tasks are coming up. author: nyx74

title: Still Has a Long Way to Go to Match Wunderlist
body:
As a very longtime daily user of Wunderlist, I recently downloaded MTD and imported my Wunderlist lists. Figured what the hey — Wunderlist is eventually going to be phased out anyway. To my surprise, MTD is missing a lot of the basic functionality that makes Wunderlist useful. 

First and foremost, when you tag a todo item with a star, it does not push that item to the top of the list. Instead you have to sort by the starred items and then manually rearrange them by dragging them around if you want to sort by priorities. This feels regressive — with Wunderlist, it was much more convenient to tap the star icon and sort your priorities that way. This feels incredibly tedious by comparison and it feels more like the application is being developed solely for desktop rather than from a mobile-first perspective. 

Also, the “daily focus” feature on MTD feels entirely useless, as other reviewers here have noted. It’s also way too tedious and unintuitive to be useful. The “starred” list view also is fundamentally flawed — instead of breaking them out into subsections by list category like Wunderlist does, it just inelegantly lumps them all into the same list. This makes that feature essentially unusable when I am using lists to manage different areas of my personal and professional life. How is it useful that my “buy milk” list item is sitting there right below my “complete TPS report” list item with no separation or context about the list they came from? Just show how little attention to detail has been put into harvesting the “best features” of Wunderlist if this one got left on the cutting room floor. 

And finally, I know this is a minor gripe that shouldn’t matter, but I really liked Wunderlist’s overall interface. You could set a background (there’s no readily apparent way to do this in MTD), it had some warm colors in the list items themselves, and the list item menus (subtasks, etc) just had an excellent user experience. I get that some of these elements may have seemed slightly skeuomorphic or frivolous to Microsoft’s dev team. By contrast, though, MTD is clunky, corporate and generally missing many of the little features and usability flourishes that I enjoyed for the past 7+ years of using Wunderlist. 

I’m also not crazy about being forced to login using a Microsoft account and integrated into that ecosystem of software — I would strongly prefer having the option of being able to just login using my existing Wunderlist credentials or a gmail account or something. 

I’m not entirely sure why Microsoft would acquire a popular app like Wunderlist and then proceed to reinvent the wheel with its own essentially inferior application. As a longtime user, I think WL deserves better than being stripped for parts and only “integrating the best features” as the Microsoft development team claims. I’d really been hoping they’d just reskin the existing application and start from that point, but I suppose that would have been too easy for a company that’s well-known for making unintuitive and over-engineered moves like this. 

Anyway, I’m going to delete the app for now and hope that more of Wunderlist’s functionality finds its way into the app before I’m ultimately forced to convert to it. Fingers crossed.

title: What I was looking for
body:
I’m a huge fan of the Outlook to-do list and to-do bar, and this app is the perfect compliment to managing productivity with Outlook. The syncing with Outlook is essential, and it’s the reason I am excited about this app.

When I’m trying to get stuff done, I’m on my phone all the time. I desperately needed a way to get and keep my tasks in front of me, which meant I needed them on my phone to do that. Microsoft To-Do was the obvious solution—I had all my flagged emails and tasks on my Outlook client; I just needed them on my phone too. 

Very happy with the smart lists and the fact that I now have ONE to do list instead of a list scratched down in a notebook, one on the fridge, one on a note-taking app, and then my list of flagged emails. 

I need to also mention the most important feature of all: the PLING you get when you check off a task. The app wouldn’t be the same without it.

title: Just forced from Wunderlist
body:
I just hired a new employee, who Wunderlist blocked from creating a new account. This forced my team to make an immediate move to To-Do, which in its current state is not as good as Wunderlist. 

We have many team members with assignments to be completed in order, but the “Assigned to You” list does not allow you to sort by due date, or any other way. 

The list provides too much detail, with little color variety, which makes it harder to find the information you need (like the due date). Wunderlist displayed this perfectly. 

The UI is clunky as well. I like to keep my list slender on one side of my laptop screen, but if you click into an item it expands the window automatically, and does not revert. 

If you are a part of a shared list your are forced to use the theme of the list owner. You cannot set your own theme in this case. 

I would have been ok with the forced transition if To-Do was an improvement, but it is not. There is a flood of improvement requests on the forum, which is discouraging. I fear my issues will not be fixed any time soon, if at all.

title: Developers Of App PLEASE READ
body:
I love the app, it beats the reminders app in some ways, so use it as my main task manager currently today. 

However, please catch up with Reminders app in these ways. 

1. Let us select pictures from photos and add it to any task, like added info to the text, but optional room n each new task created.

2. The main screen where you can make a folder, or just see the individual task categories you make, give is the ability to change the symbol on the left hand side to hundreds of symbols to choose from. Also let us change the color of the symbols. This helps users visualize where they need to go quicker when opening the app, and more easy to use and manage list of we have lots of categories. 

3. Give us the ability to love around and hide the default list at the top, so app is easier to use. That way it’s like a “desktop” computer, think of it that way. If we don’t use a feature much on windows desktop, we probably don’t want a “shortcut” link to that app that we cannot move or hide always there. So ability to hide default list if can’t delete them. 

4. Also please add a feature, kind of goes with number 3, to let us change the theme of the home screen of the app. This way we can choose how to “visualize” our list on a way that best works for a user, since everyone is different. 

5. Last several times I have list shared to me, and they would get an error. We would try again the next day and normally no problems second time. 

6. Would be cool to be able to add voice memos as well to a specific task. 

Thank you, love the app, just think would be number one app in world in take in these ideas.

title: The most important app on my phone
body:
I picked up this app on my iPhone and Mac, hoping I could work it into my routine at work and solve some of my team’s productivity and communication issues. To Do quickly became the lifeline of my business in exactly the way I had hoped, by organizing all of our messy actions and projects across multiple lists shared among various team members. In addition to typical tools in the toolbox, such as “Reminder,” “Due Date,” “Steps” and others, the addition of “My Day” and “Assign To” are unique to me tools I use every single day.  

To Do is incredibly simple to use and understand. In addition to work, I’ve been using it as well for my personal life, and other professional projects and volunteer work. Doing this has only strengthened my commitment to it, while my past experience with to do apps was almost always short-lived. 

Few other apps, if any, bring a simplified, high level of organization and teamwork to productivity as this one does- at a cost of nothing. 

I’m looking forward to updates with new features and further integration with Outlook and other Microsoft tools, but right now, this is already the best and most important app I use, hands down!

title: It’s like it was made by someone who never uses these things
body:
I’m trying to embrace change, having been a lifetime Wunderlist user, but some of the behavior here is downright bizarre. I don’t feel like this is even a lateral move.

First off, having tasks scheduled for TODAY’S date should force them into the ‘My Day’ list. This seems like default behavior to me. Having to manually search for and add them is counterproductive. 

What happens to tasks I move to ‘My Day’ that aren’t completed and become overdue?  Tomorrow they’re just... gone. Poof! 

The tasks on the ‘planned’ and ‘important’ screens should be grouped by the parent list. It feels incoherent.  Many tasks don’t make sense when they’re orphaned from their parent.

Overall the app seems a bit half-baked, I’m disappointed.

title: Almost as good as Wunderlist
body:
Microsoft has done a good job replacing Wunderlist (which they bought) with To Do, and making it pretty easy to migrate from Wunderlist to To Do. Overall, functionality is everything you’d need to manage your tasks. 

Things to improve: 

1. Make it easier to migrate from Wunderlist WITH people you previously shared lists with. It took my wife and me an hour to figure that out. Not a great way to get started. 

2. Allow users to set default order for new tasks. Currently they always go to the bottom of the list. I’d prefer to have them go to the top, like I could do in Wunderlist. 

3. If you accidentally drop a task onto another task, it will turn it into a sub task. Not a bad feature, except that you can’t drag that sub task back “up” to turn it back into a task.  Or if you can, it’s not at all obvious how to do so. 

4. Moving tasks between lists is cumbersome. You can’t just drag and drop it, like you could on Wunderlist. You have to Edit the list, then move it. Extra clicks, and unintuitive, ugh.
